findings.description: Test adequacy: no test has a changed file whose path matches a rule but whose content does not, so dropping the content regex (warn whenever the path matches) passes the whole suite.
Test adequacy: no quality-checks test deletes a tracked source file, so removing the `Path::new(file).is_file()` filter (which would hand the deleted path to the lint) passes the suite.

The Rust check tells the agent to seal with `.claude/hooks/comment-pruner.sh seal`, but that script writes SHA-256 hashes while the Rust check reads raw comment text. Once settings.json runs `claude-hooks comment-pruner`, the seal it asks for can never match, so the same comments re-dispatch the pruner every turn until a commit. stop_hook_active only limits this to one dispatch per Stop cycle. Nothing is rewired in this PR, so this cannot happen yet; the message (and the test that checks it, tests/comment_pruner.rs:45) needs to point at the binary's own seal by the time it is wired.

The port drops the shell's `[ -f "$f" ]` check on untracked files. An untracked symlink with a source extension pointing at `/dev/zero`, `/dev/urandom` or a FIFO makes the unsandboxed Stop hook read without limit (memory exhaustion) or hang until the hook timeout. The shell version skipped non-regular targets.

Untracked files are appended with no separator (`added.extend(std::fs::read(file)...)`), so a file with no trailing newline joins its last line to the next file's first line. A sealed trailing comment can then come back as 'new' when only the other file is edited, causing one spurious dispatch (the shell's `cat` loop behaves the same).

The shell hook matched a rule's content field with GNU `grep -E`, which treats an unescaped `{` that cannot start a valid interval as a literal. regex-lite rejects it, and `Regex::new(content).ok()?` then drops the whole rule with no message. A `spot-checks.tsv` rule written to the file's documented "content ERE (grep -E)" contract, such as `catch[[:space:]]*\(.*\)[[:space:]]*{[[:space:]]*}`, fired under the shell hook and silently never fires under the port. Either escape a `{` that is not followed by a digit, or state in the TSV header that patterns use regex-lite syntax.
The deleted `src/gone.ts` holds no violation, so the test's claim that a deleted file is skipped cannot fail (the `is_file` guard in convention_spot_check.rs line 70 is untested).
The new `xargs` emulation has no test: batching at 5000 files or 128 KiB, a failure in one batch not stopping later ones, the 255 abort, and the both-commands-empty early return are all untouched.

The new `script()` helper is identical to the existing `common::executable` (write the file, then chmod 0o755). Delete it, call `executable` at its 2 call sites (L58, L199), and drop the `PermissionsExt` import. -6 +0.
`Fixture::path_with` re-implements the existing `common::path_with`, and the old-git test stacks a second hand-built `format!` PATH on top of it. Use `common::path_with` in both places. About -9 +2.
`write` followed by `set_permissions(0o755)` is what `common::executable` already does. Call it instead and drop `PermissionsExt` from the imports. -3 +1.

`failing_lint_exits_2_with_at_most_40_output_lines` and `failing_lint_prints_the_last_40_lines_then_the_verdict` run the same failing-lint path. The second already pins stderr exactly (lines 161-200 plus the verdict), which implies "at most 40". Keep the second, add its missing exit-code check, and delete the first. -12 +1.

`format!("{}{}", out.stdout, out.stderr)` re-implements the existing `Output::text()` in `tests/common/mod.rs`; the same pattern sits in tests/convention_spot_check.rs:65 and tests/post_compact_state.rs:167, and the two `assert_silent` copies are byte-identical. Use `out.text()`; optionally move `assert_silent` into `common` (about -4).
The `is_check` pre-scan repeats the comment and blank filtering that the `rules` parse (L45-61) already does. Parse first, then return when `rules.is_empty() || stop_hook_active()`. About -3 +1.

The unsandboxed comment-pruner Stop hook runs a porcelain `git diff HEAD --unified=0` without `--no-ext-diff`/`--no-textconv` (as `check_dashes.rs` already passes), so a `diff.external` or textconv driver from the checkout's git config runs outside the sandbox; the index reads at L95/L99 can also run fsmonitor. The shell original does the same.

process_issues.description: review-quality reported reading only session.rs and the four new src modules: it did not read the new test files against docs/conventions/testing.md and did not list or read docs/adr/, so test-file convention and ADR conformance went unaudited this round.
